limitations: CPU data integration only; no model training or accelerator qualification.
One-second process-memory samples are lower bounds; filesystem page cache is not included.
Cache-byte limit excludes row-bounded pending results, decoder temporaries, and processor residency.
cpu_preprocessing.timing_scope: CPU preprocessing passes; not training throughput; uncontrolled filesystem cache

higher_precision_cpu_regression.scope: Tiny real Qwen3.5 native FP32 text/image/video SFT, two updates and resume from the first update.

measurement_definitions: All memory values are bytes. Divide by 2^30 for GiB. Missing values remain null.
Torch phase peaks are allocator peaks recorded before each explicit reset. All-phase peaks include loading, validation, training and synchronous checkpoint work in the uninterrupted process.

Loading is the interval ending adapter_loading_complete; first/later updates end optimizer_step_N; checkpoint-write intervals end checkpoint_complete and begin at checkpoint_begin. These intervals may include associated native CPU work.
Host HWM from phase records is the trainer process lifetime high-water mark, not a per-phase reset metric.

NVML device and owned-compute-process values use only matching device UUID samples with run-owned processes and valid bounded memory. One-second samples are lower bounds; device totals can include non-run allocations.
Selected-run host RSS/PSS sums include launcher, trainer and worker processes. Process RSS/PSS/HWM excludes unmapped filesystem page-cache memory.
Compiled first-forward diagnostics subtract preflight counters and establish native capture/reuse. They do not establish complete fusion or attribute saved training tensors.
Each configuration has exact same-configuration resume/reload evidence; this does not imply exact equivalence across different arithmetic, checkpointing or microbatch configurations.
The shape audit replays ordered native data on CPU and matches both historical final cursors. It is not input telemetry captured during the GPU training run.
Four-update canary peaks and pass timings do not establish sustained throughput, held-out task quality or support for untested hardware/topologies.
scope: Thirteen single-device four-update lifecycle canaries, kernel tests, CPU preprocessing/regression and a historical training-input replay. No release quality or throughput qualification.

shared_cuda_kernel_gate.test_scope: Real accelerator quantization/adapter/checkpointing/compile forward-backward tests, including strict deterministic Flash SDPA.

training_shape_replay.frame_count_interpretation: Temporal slots are inferred from grid time times temporal patch size; source frame indices/timestamps were not recorded.
limitations: CPU preprocessing replay, not telemetry captured during model training or a throughput benchmark.

The ordered 2400 rows and final data cursor match both historical 300-update checkpoints. Historical microbatch1/accumulation8 had different physical padding from this microbatch4/accumulation2 audit.
Processed temporal frame slots include any processor temporal padding or repeated sampled source frames; they are not a count of unique source frames.
Host process HWM excludes unmapped filesystem page-cache memory; cache cap excludes decoder temporaries and current batch tensors.
Derived from completed CPU native preprocessing replay and pinned no-alignment collator; not runtime training input telemetry.
Historical runs used microbatch1/accumulation8; the replay directly measured microbatch4/accumulation2 and preserves identical ordered rows.
Logical input lengths do not describe internal GPU-kernel tile padding or predict total model memory.
